article.title: Acusativo: в dirección
article.chapter: Acusativo y animacidad — Винительный падеж и одушевлённость

claims.summary: The Russian preposition 'в' can combine with accusative case to indicate direction towards the interior of a place or towards a destination.

With movement verbs, 'в + accusative' signals the destination of the displacement. The preposition 'в' governs the nominal group and determines the accusative case here. It should not be confused with 'в + prepositivo', which usually indicates location without movement towards the interior.

Examples provided include 'Я иду в школу' ('I go to school'), 'Мы едем в Москву' ('We go to Moscow'), and 'Дети вошли в комнату' ('The children entered the room'), all of which demonstrate the use of 'в' with accusative case to indicate direction.

Not all uses of 'в' involve accusative case. For instance, 'Я иду в школу' (I go to school) indicates direction, while 'Я в школе' (I am in the school) indicates location and uses preposition, not accusative.
